MARKET.head: Australian white wine shipments to China more than double in Q3
MARKET.summ: White wine export volumes to the market more than doubled, rising 143.6%, according to Wine Australia data. The growth comes as Australian producers seek a greater foothold among Chinese white wine drinkers, including consumers exploring alternatives to Burgundy
takeaways: Australian wine export value to mainland China rose 1.9% to A$166.33 million in Q3 2026, bucking a global decline.
White wine export volume to mainland China jumped 143.6% to 5.26 million liters, while white wine value rose 51.9%.
Mainland China's Q3 gain still left nine-month export value down 10.4% to A$758.59 million.

MARKET.head: Hampshire wineries Chalkdown and The B58 launch joint celebration wine collective
MARKET.summ: Chalkdown English Sparkling Wine and The B58 Winery, two of Hampshire’s independent winemakers, are launching the Hampshire Celebration Collective, a new partnership created to bring local wines to the county’s
takeaways: Chalkdown English Sparkling Wine and The B58 Winery, two Hampshire producers, are launching the Hampshire Celebration Collective partnership.
The Collective offers bespoke pricing per order, a one-case minimum, and mix-and-match wines across both producers.
Launch is a free tasting at Kingsgate Wines & Provisions in Winchester, Thursday 19 November, 5pm to 7pm, with an on-the-night discount.

MARKET.head: Shanghai wine trader WINEXSH files for bankruptcy liquidation amid falling prices
MARKET.summ: Shanghai-based fine wine trader WINEXSH has applied for bankruptcy liquidation, with a supplier reporting an unpaid order and Chinese wine media citing complaints from customers unable to collect wines or secure refunds
takeaways: Shanghai fine wine trader WINEXSH applied for bankruptcy liquidation, with a Shanghai Pudong court reviewing the application.
A supplier reported an unpaid en primeur order, and consumers reported delayed collections and refunds.
The company, founded in 2012, had built large inventories that lost value as Chinese fine wine prices declined.

MARKET.head: Western Australian wineries sell on the spot at Shanghai festival
MARKET.summ: A two-day Discover Western Australian Festival drew nearly 900 people in Shanghai, with exhibitors reporting stronger-than-expected consumer sales and new business prospects among distributors, restaurants and hotels
takeaways: Discover Western Australia Festival in Shanghai on November 7-8 drew nearly 900 visitors, including about 600 consumers and 300 trade professionals.
Twenty exhibitors, including 17 wineries from Margaret River and Great Southern, sold wines on site and attracted distributor and hotel interest.
Ferngrove sold flagship wines through Red Note during the event, and Pran Wines reported strong interest in lesser-known 3 Drops.

MARKET.head: Wine Australia and Wine Victoria partner on three-year Victorian wine projects
MARKET.summ: A new partnership between Wine Australia and Wine Victoria will fund a range of projects across the Victorian wine industry supporting grapegrowers and winemakers.
takeaways: Wine Australia and Wine Victoria will co-fund Victorian wine industry projects over three years, aligned with the Victorian Wine Strategy 2025-2030.
The program combines $540,000 in Victorian Government funding secured by Wine Victoria with $346,667 from Wine Australia's AWFF.
Projects will cover sustainability, biosecurity preparedness, data-driven decisions and export capability, delivered through workshops, webinars and benchmarking tools.

MARKET.head: Wine remains Australia's most bought alcohol category as drinking moderates
MARKET.summ: New research shows that wine endures as “the most widely purchased category” in Australia at 55%, followed by spirits at 46% and beer at 44%. The new ‘What’s Driving Australia’s Alcohol Shopper: Consumption, Channels, Promotions and Occasions’ report from Vypr and Shop! ANZ found that 41% of Australians are drinking less than a...
takeaways: Vypr and Shop! ANZ report: 55% of Australians buy wine, ahead of spirits at 46% and beer at 44%.
41% of Australians drink less than a year ago or have stopped, while only 6% drink more.
48% of shoppers now typically spend over $40 per liquor-store visit, up from about 23% a year ago.

MARKET.head: Marnong Estate releases first Reserve Chardonnay alongside new spring range
MARKET.summ: Marnong Estate has unveiled its first-ever Reserve Chardonnay as a part its new collection of cool-climate expressions from the estate's Sunbury vineyards. The 2024 Reserve Chardonnay leads the new range which features the 2025 Single Vineyard Chardonnay and 2025 Estate Chardonnay, offering “distinct interpretations of the...
takeaways: Marnong Estate, a Sunbury winery, has released its first-ever Reserve Chardonnay, the 2024 vintage, as part of a new range.
The spring collection also includes the 2025 Single Vineyard Chardonnay, the 2025 Estate Chardonnay and the 2026 Estate Sangiovese Rosé.
The wines are sold nationally through independent merchants, at the cellar door and online via the winery's website.

MARKET.head: Moldova pitches indigenous grapes and 23 producers to Chinese buyers at ProWine Shanghai
MARKET.summ: With 23 wine and spirits producers heading to ProWine Shanghai, the export-driven country is putting indigenous grapes and competitive pricing at the center of its pitch
takeaways: The National Office for Vine and Wine is bringing 23 Moldovan producers to ProWine Shanghai from November 10 to 12 to seek Chinese importers.
Moldova's wine imports to China reached US$1.43 million in the first nine months of 2026, per Chinese customs data.
About 85% of Moldovan wine production is exported, and the EU now takes roughly 60% of those exports.

MARKET.head: Australian wine packaging sees growth in small formats for convenience and moderation
MARKET.summ: Consumer demand for wine is changing globally, and while this has shown up in many mature markets as a decline in consumption, the shift in consumption habits has also uncovered an increasing consumer interest in smaller, more flexible packaging formats.
takeaways: Combined export and domestic off-trade sales of 187mL wine packs rose 22% to almost 1.9 million litres in 2025-26.
Export volumes of 187mL packs grew 39%, from 450,000 litres in 2023-24 to 620,000 litres in 2025-26.
Australian single-person households reached 26% of households, up from 18% in 1981, per Census data cited by the Market Bulletin.

MARKET.head: EU greenwashing directive bans vague eco claims on wine from September 27
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: EU Directive 2024/825, enforced from September 27, bans vague environmental claims like "eco-friendly" and "green" on products including wine.
Unverified sustainability badges and misleading claims are prohibited, with old stock not grandfathered in, so producers are using stickers or point-of-sale notices.
Member states set enforcement, with fines up to four percent of annual turnover for widespread violations, and wine producers must also avoid such claims in marketing.

CULTURE.head: ASVO names 2026 Viticulturist and Winemaker of the Year at awards dinner
CULTURE.summ: Last night, the Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology (ASVO) revealed the winners of its Awards for Excellence. The ASVO said the winners were chosen from a very high calibre and diverse range of submissions showing expertise across winemaking, viticulture and wine science. Highlights of the evening included the naming...
takeaways: Chris Dent, owner of Gorton Drive Estate and chair of Murray Valley Winegrowers, was named ASVO 2026 Viticulturist of the Year.
David Bicknell, of Oakridge Wines, was named 2026 Winemaker of the Year after almost 25 years at the winery.
Tracey Siebert of the AWRI won the Wine Science and Technology Award for her flavour chemistry and aroma research.

CULTURE.head: AI's energy, e-waste and water footprint threatens wine's sustainability image
CULTURE.summ: The Australian and New Zealand wine sector prides itself on sustainability. The very concept has become the industry’s bread and butter, quite frankly. Look at any winery website and you’ll find a dedicated page filled with paragraphs detailing all the initiatives reducing carbon emissions, saving water and limiting energy use...
takeaways: Australian and New Zealand wine sector promotes sustainability, but AI-generated content in its marketing and labels risks undermining that clean reputation.
One study estimated training a single large language model emits around 300,000 kg of CO₂, roughly the emissions of 105 cars driven 15,000 km a year.
Global data centres are estimated to consume 945 terawatt-hours of electricity by 2030, with AI accounting for 40% of that demand.

CULTURE.head: Marlborough viticulture technician Anna Kelland wins 2026 Young Horticulturist of the Year
CULTURE.summ: Marlborough viticulture technician Anna Kelland has won the Young Horticulturist of the Year title, having “excelled” in an intensive two-day competition in Auckland from 4-5 November. Kelland was the 2025 New Zealand Young Viticulturist of the Year and therefore went through to represent the viticulture sector in this year’s...
takeaways: Anna Kelland, a viticulture technician for Constellation Brands in Marlborough, won the Young Horticulturist of the Year title in Auckland.
She beat four rivals from grower, arborist, amenity and plant producer sectors over a two-day competition held 4-5 November.
Her prizes, including three awards, a scholarship and a glass trophy, total more than $25,000 in cash and value.

SCIENCE.head: Burgundy estate uses electrical conductivity mapping to guide soil digging
SCIENCE.summ: Electrical conductivity maps can reveal striking differences beneath seemingly uniform vineyards, but understanding what those differences mean is far more complicated
takeaways: Domaine du Cellier aux Moines in Givry, Burgundy, used electrical conductivity (EC) mapping from 2021 to guide over 30 soil pits.
Pits revealed large differences in limestone density about 1.5 metres down, much less visible from the surface.
In the 2026 vintage, a tressed Pinot Noir parcel reached 13.6% potential alcohol versus 14.5% for a conventionally trimmed neighbour.

NEWSLETTERS.summ: There’s the glamorous side of the wine industry: the landscape, the people, the amazing farming and craftsmanship that goes into
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Portuguese mini-study: four red wines from Casa Ferreirinha, Quinta Nova, Douorum and Rocim
NEWSLETTERS.summ: These four Portuguese reds were all purchased from supermarket Pingo Doce and an independent wine shop, while I was teaching
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Casa Ferreirinha Vinha Grande 2023 Douro scored 92/100 and costs about €12 in Portugal, roughly £17 in the UK.
Quinta Nova de Nossa Senhora do Carmo Unoaked 2024 Douro, a Touriga Nacional-led blend, scored 93/100 at €16.90 in Vila Real.
Pingo Doce's private label Tons de Duorum Talhão 37 2024 Douro, made by Duorum, scored 91/100 at €6.99 down from €13.99.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Five Minutes with... Rick Rainey & Léana Godard of Forge Cellars
NEWSLETTERS.summ: On Cabernet Franc’s untapped potential, giving Finger Lakes terroir a seat at the table, and why it’s all about joy
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Forge Cellars, founded 2011 on Seneca Lake in New York's Finger Lakes, began making Cabernet Franc with the 2019 vintage.
Forge now makes four single-vineyard Cabernet Francs from different soils, including Willow (sand), Railroad (gravel), Arlo (clay) and Bellows (sand and rock).
In 2023 Forge left stems out entirely to study each site's tannin potential, then reintroduced stems in some wines in 2024.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Kitchen Season’s Pantry Staples
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Stocking up before the cooking starts in earnest; plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker's Maker's Table piece lists pantry staples for the holiday cooking and baking season, following her earlier kitchen tools list in The Salt.
She advises checking pantry shelves in mid-November, since baking ingredients do not last indefinitely.
Spices and herbs should be refreshed regularly and bought in small quantities from bulk aisles, and baking chemicals renewed regularly.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Sixteen Austrian Wines You Should Try
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Delicious recommendations,including old favourites and new discoveries
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Austrian wine editor's masterclass in Daejeon, South Korea covered 60 wine professionals, and a tasting in Amsterdam hosted 40 somms, journalists and importers.
The author tasted 72 wines to select 16 favourites, all herbicide-free and mostly organic or biodynamic certified.
Fischer's 2025 Sauvignon Blanc St. Anna, made by brothers Klaus and Bernard, is recommended, priced at €25 from Joost Wijn in the Netherlands.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues that wine critics should be only slightly more knowledgeable than their target audience, not overly expert.
Atkin says conflicts of interest matter beyond payments, such as dining, friendships and shared politics, and that disclosure can encourage self-interested views.
Atkin criticises the 30-second wine tasting ritual, often done across dozens or over a hundred wines, as too brief to assess a wine properly.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Meet the Young Winemakers Reshaping Burgundy Right Now
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Meet the young winemakers in the heart of Burgundy who are tending the vines and shaping the future of wine
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: William Whitehead runs Domaine Michel Rebourgeon in Pommard, which works 4.25 hectares across Pommard, Volnay and Beaune and makes about 20,000 bottles a year.
Pierre Arcelain's Domaine Michel Arcelain ages its white wine for 12 months in a concrete egg, a modern tool the new generation has adopted.
Julien Cruchandeau, a newcomer from hospitality, founded his estate in 2003 and moved to Chaux in 2009, championing Aligoté and Hautes-Côtes de Nuits.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources like local-language catalogues, merchant inventories, auction and consignment notices, and restaurant sales.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions or images, and Orpheus notifies them when matching wine is available in its network.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine in 1872 in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, Penedès, Catalonia.
Cava takes its name from the cellars, or caves, dug to store the wine, and became a formal Spanish label term in 1972.
Sumarroca Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava 2022 from Penedès is made from Macabeu, Xarel•lo and Parellada and aged 40 months.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing and was set to visit Guangzhou on November 6.
Spain ranked fifth for wine volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy and a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
Spain's value ranking in China dropped to sixth, below New Zealand and above only Chile among the top eight sources.
